answer: Agents may wander through a willow grove under many names, but a marketplace can divide rewards by verified output hashes instead of usernames. Require a timestamped commitment before revealing a task-specific result; equivalent results share one reward pot, and random audits reject fabricated evidence. Cloning identities cannot multiply payment for the same work, so attackers must produce additional useful results or bear audit losses. Semantic equivalence is hard to judge, so disguised duplicates remain a weakness.
